The show also covers major gaming news from BlizzCon, highlighting the expansion of World of Warcraft, and features a segment on the controversial 'analog hole' initiative. The episode concludes with a performance by beatboxer Kid Beyond and a showcase of viewer-submitted content.

notes.title: John Dykstra, Giant NES Gamepad, Reel Big Fish
notes.summary: An early Attack of the Show with Kevin Pereira, Kevin Rose, Sarah Lane and Brendan Moran. The centerpiece is an in-studio interview with Academy Award-winning visual effects pioneer John Dykstra, who talks about Star Wars, building the Caddyshack gopher, the emotional VFX work on Spider-Man, and his prediction of composite CGI actors. Elsewhere Kevin drives around town discovering the PSP launch was not the sellout everyone expected, Kevin Rose unveils an eight-foot 'world's largest Nintendo controller' built from a gutted NES pad, and the crew reviews Lego Star Wars as a buy. The Feed covers the Immersion rumble-pad injunction against Sony, Mark Cuban bankrolling Grokster ahead of MGM v. Grokster, and the 70-million-year-old T. rex soft tissue find. Ska punk band Reel Big Fish closes the show with a live performance.

notable.text: Kevin Rose demos the self-proclaimed world's largest Nintendo controller: eight feet long, three and a half feet wide, built by three people in 20 hours for about $400.
Field piece documents that the PSP was NOT sold out at US retail on launch week, undercutting the expected iPod-of-the-year hype.
The Feed reports the discovery of elastic soft tissue and blood vessels in a 70 million year old T. rex fossil, overturning the belief that soft tissue could not survive past 100,000 years.
A judge ordered Sony to pay $90 million and halt PlayStation sales over Immersion's rumble feedback patent, pending appeal.
Kevin teases that tomorrow's show will 'serve a website out of someone's ass' as a TV and internet first.

notes.summary: Kevin Pereira and Sarah Lane open with PSP homebrew hacking, using Wipeout Pure's built-in browser and a spoofed DNS server to get IRC running on the two-week-old handheld, then gawk at Japan's Land Walker mech. They call back to the Star Wars fans camped at Grauman's Chinese Theatre who refuse to believe Revenge of the Sith is actually opening at the ArcLight. Now Playing Magazine editor-in-chief Eric Morrow pitches his new pop-culture title and predicts video-game-to-film adaptations and live-action anime as the next big trends, followed by a comedy 'prison tech' satellite interview demonstrating a battery lighter, a shiv and a homemade tattoo gun. A Sport Vision field piece explains how the football yellow line, the glowing hockey puck, baseball's K-Zone and NASCAR car telemetry work, and Justin Keeling shows off Japanese DS imports Pac-Pix and Touch Kirby. The show closes with The Feed, the movie-poster User Created submissions and a mini review of the Dell Inspiron XPS Gen 2.

News of the day: a Texarkana shop's click-fraud lawsuit against Google, Yahoo, AOL and others over pay-per-click advertising.
Coverage of the first-ever photograph of a planet outside our solar system, taken with Hubble and two ground telescopes.
Flickr began deleting photos tagged AOTS in response to the show's viral 'pee in the Flickr pools' art experiment, so the hosts told viewers to stop tagging.

notes.title: deviantART.com, Tomb Raider Fan Film, Dennis "Thresh" Fong
notes.summary: Kevin Pereira, Sarah Lane and Kevin Rose open with Kevin Rose delivering his very first AOTS show intro, then dig into the Our Colony ARG that fans believe teases the next Xbox. Kevin Rose builds a do-it-yourself gas mask out of a CPU fan, tubing and a floppy cleaning disc as a $200 commercial alternative, and later pits two CD/DVD scratch-repair machines against deliberately gouged copies of Catwoman. notes.summary: Kevin Pereira, Kevin Rose, Sarah Lane and Brendan Moran host an episode built around a long in-studio visit from director John Milius, who is consulting and writing on EA's Medal of Honor: European Assault. Milius argues games will eventually carry month-long, novel-length stories, confirms Warner Bros. has shelved King Conan, and says he was flattered to be the model for The Big Lebowski's Walter; he later returns to take viewer phone calls about the hand-built Red Dawn tanks and the game's Stalingrad and Ardennes settings. The Feed reports Paramount definitively cancelled Star Trek: Enterprise despite a fan campaign that raised over $3 million.

notes.summary: A Star Wars-heavy Monday episode hosted by Kevin Pereira, Kevin Rose, Sarah Lane and Brendan Moran. Blur Studio founder Tim Miller and supervisor Jeff Fowler visit to explain how the studio went from game cinematics to an Academy Award nomination for the short Gopher Broke, and preview their E3 work on Hellgate, Company of Heroes and Aeon Flux. Cool Hunting's Josh Rubin and Carol Chong explain the design blog and her Atari-sponsored Retro Redux game jam winner Ninja Garden. notes.title: Engadget.com, Media Players, LAN Party
notes.summary: Engadget founder Peter Rojas is the featured guest, explaining how the site runs editors around the clock to post 30-50 stories a day, defending blog ethics against print-magazine embargoes, and revealing that Microsoft called him up to offer a half hour with Bill Gates. He returns later to take live viewer calls from Dallas, Indiana and Massachusetts, and admits he left Gizmodo, which he founded, to get editorial freedom at Engadget. Kevin Rose runs down a list of free open-source Windows software and reviews the Archos Pocket Media Assistant and Creative Zen Portable Media Center as portable video ahead of an expected Apple device. The Thursday LAN party plays Call of Duty: United Offensive with Surf Illustrated models Lindsay and Chantel, and a LucasArts featurette shows stunt coordinator Nick Gillard and Hayden Christensen training animators for the Revenge of the Sith game. The Feed covers GameSpy secretly rewriting a freelancer's Donkey Konga 2 review, iris scanners at Orlando airport, and Google's purchase of Dodgeball, while the show signs off for a week of live E3 coverage.

notes.title: Jake Bronstein, Drunk Vader, Chris Gore
notes.summary: Back from a week of E3 coverage, Kevin Rose uses the top of the show to announce he is leaving G4 - the network released him from his four-year contract - to make Systm, a downloadable web show he is launching with old TechTV friends, with Friday as his last day. Kevin Pereira recaps E3, the never-shipping Phantom console and the Photoshopped PS3 'grill', then re-airs his Drunk Vader field piece from the Revenge of the Sith premiere line. FHM editor at large Jake Bronstein visits to talk up the magazine's Beth Ostrosky cover, its girl-next-door formula and the Video Game Vixens contest, while It Came From eBay digs up Star Wars sock monkeys, a bull penis walking stick and a hobo fantasy camp. Sarah Lane's Feed covers Alan Moore severing ties with DC, an early data-hostage ransomware worm, and the MPAA blaming BitTorrent for the Sith leak; Chris Gore returns for DVDuesday on Chappelle's Show Season 2, The Aviator and Super Friends, and Sarah's Damn Good Download is MediaMan 2.

notes.title: Ze Frank, Mario Opera, User Created
notes.summary: Kevin Pereira, Sarah Lane and a departing Kevin Rose spend the week's penultimate show on web culture and civil liberties. Internet performance artist Ze Frank explains how a birthday-invite dance video sent to seventeen friends turned into a million hits a day and roughly forty million viewers, then demos his participatory projects and joke video games. Kevin Rose delivers his final Dark Tip, a homemade self-scanning war-spying rig with a cantenna that pulls unencrypted X10 camera feeds out of homes and hotel rooms. The EFF's Danny O'Brien joins by phone to warn about a closed-door Senate push to expand the Patriot Act, Atari producer Kyle Peschel demos TimeShift's time-rewinding gunplay, and the show reviews the PalmOne LifeDrive and airs viewer-made AOTS arcade cabinet designs.

notable.text: Kevin Rose's final Dark Tip segment, marking the end of the recurring franchise as he leaves the show.

Howard Stern played Kevin Pereira's FHM interview about Beth Ostrosky on his radio show and responded on air.
A Minnesota judge allowed the mere presence of encryption software on a defendant's computer to be entered as evidence of criminal activity.
The Feed marks the deaths of three cartoon voice legends in one week: Henry Corden (Fred Flintstone), Howard Morris (Jet Screamer) and Thurl Ravenscroft (Tony the Tiger).

notes.summary: Kevin Pereira opens raving about Will Wright's newly posted GDC demo video for Spore, then shows off Broadcast Machine, an open-source PHP tool for publishing RSS- and BitTorrent-wrapped web video channels, followed by a gallery of accidentally phallic corporate logos and the ML iPod WinAmp plugin for iPod owners who hate iTunes. Robert Hamburger, creator of RealUltimatePower.net, comes on to explain that he is not in fact a ten-year-old boy and to tell the story of how a publisher bought his official ninja book after an executive flipped it open to a drawing of a ninja with an enormous erection. Internet personality Jessica Chobot joins the Unreal Tournament 2004 LAN party, explains that her famous PSP-licking photo was a joke that people mistook for Sony viral marketing, and identifies a PSP, a DS and an N-Gage blindfolded by taste. notes.title: Max Cannon, Leveling Up. PINE*am
notes.summary: This is Kevin Rose's final episode of Attack of the Show after about three and a half years on TechTV and G4, and his family is in the studio audience. The crew tests the grey market around World of Warcraft, buying a $101 power-leveling service that takes their level 7 mage to level 23 in three days, and surveys eBay listings where level 60 accounts sell for hundreds of dollars. Cartoonist Max Cannon visits to promote Red Meat Gold, and an encore of the 'Seduced by Science' mockumentary hunts the swag-obsessed 'Gnerd' at E3 2005. The Feed covers a Georgia high school paper shut down over its stories, TorrentSpy blocking Star Wars and Family Guy searches under the DMCA, and 1984 Q*bert champion Doris Self training with Billy Mitchell for a comeback. Japanese techno pop trio Pine*am performs 'Get a Choco', and the show closes with a 2002 Screen Savers clip of a much younger Kevin Rose demonstrating a port scan.

notes.title: Greg Costikyan, Mark Hamill, GreaseMonkey
notes.summary: X-Play's Adam Sessler returns for a second day co-hosting with Kevin Pereira and Sarah Lane. The web roundup covers a leaked EB Games list pegging Xbox 360 titles at $59.99, a PC case built entirely from 70 cooling fans, and a live call to CallTheInternet.org, where an operator named Kyle patiently describes LimeCat.net to the hosts over the phone. Kevin gives an extended tutorial on Greasemonkey and Platypus, showing user scripts that strip ads from Boing Boing and Fark and add cross-site price comparison to Amazon. Game designer Greg Costikian argues that ballooning development budgets have made publishers too risk-averse for innovation, and a taped Mark Hamill interview covers Super Robot Monkey Team Hyperforce Go!, his Joker work and the Star Wars prequels. EA's Dan Winters demos Medal of Honor: European Assault's open battlefields, squad control and adrenaline mode, and the show closes with a racing wheel roundup and user-created AOTS CD cases.

notes.title: Eric Nakamura, Dial-A-Song, LAN Party
notes.summary: Engadget founder Peter Rojas guest hosts alongside Kevin Pereira, Sarah Lane and Brendan Moran. The centerpiece is Diddy Bot, an Attack of the Show original Mac hack built with AppleScript, Automator, Soundflower and Skype that lets you text a song title and have iTunes call your cell phone and play it back; it works on air, though viewers immediately dial the phone number and interrupt the segment. notes.title: Jason Kottke, AWOL Vaporizer, Civilization IV
notes.summary: Tina Wood guest hosts with Kevin Pereira and Sarah Lane, opening with Oakley Thump MP3 sunglasses, an OS X Finder skin for Windows Explorer, an archive of Sega Genesis startup logos, and the Biblical Curse Generator. NVIDIA product manager Jason Paul brings in the just-launched GeForce 7800 GTX, demoing the Luna tech demo and Battlefield 2 in SLI with near-2x scaling, and confirms the card shares its parent architecture with the PlayStation 3's RSX chip. Brendan Moran field-tests the $300 AWOL alcohol vaporizer and gets visibly wrecked, while Firaxis's Jesse Smith previews Civilization IV's 3D engine, religions, Great People, and Python/XML modding ahead of its November release. Blogger Jason Kottke explains how he quit his design job and funded a full year of kottke.org through a three-week PayPal reader drive, and recounts Sony's cease and desist over his leaked Ken Jennings Jeopardy clip. notes.summary: Adam Sessler guest hosts the week with Kevin Pereira, opening on Yahoo's My Web 2.0 social bookmarking beta, an Atari homebrew remake called Adventure II, a Maria Sharapova grunt ringtone, and a time-lapse video of a Lego Star Wars Star Destroyer being built. DIG! director Ondi Timoner describes shooting roughly 2,000 hours over seven years to chronicle Anton Newcombe's Brian Jonestown Massacre and Courtney Taylor's Dandy Warhols, and shows footage of BJM imploding on stage at the Viper Room in front of nine record labels. notes.summary: Adam Sessler and Kevin Pereira co-host with Sarah Lane freshly back from New York. Paul Berry explains the Contagious Media Showdown, a three-week contest to see which purpose-built website could generate the most traffic, which ForgetMeNotPanties.com won after Blogebrity and Crying While Eating led early; Kevin recounts AOTS's own viral experiment, Geek Fantasies. notes.summary: Newgrounds founder Tom Fulp guest hosts alongside Kevin Pereira, Sarah Lane and Brendan Moran. The tech centerpiece is installing Linux on a first-through-third-generation iPod to play video, complete with a live command-line encode, though the hack still has no sound. The show also covers the intense debate between game art and interactive experience with developer David Jaffe, who discusses the challenges of the industry and the rise of next-gen consoles like the PS3 and Xbox 360. Field reports from the San Francisco Game Conference showcase various titles, while the segment also includes political humor regarding Saddam Hussein and a look at viewer-submitted content.

notable.text: David Jaffe argues that the true potential of games as art lies in the interactive experience itself, not just in cutscenes.
The Machinima Film Festival features a discussion on the technical line between a game engine and a rendered movie, exemplified by 'Person 2184'.
The show highlights the growing trend of blog culture, noting a poll that found only four percent of German internet users regularly conversed via blogs.

notes.title: Morgan Spurlock, Death Jr., Amtrak Mooning
notes.summary: Kevin Pereira hosts with CNET's Will O'Neal filling in and Sarah Lane on the couch, opening with Stuffonmycat.com, the Halo 2 machinima talk show This Spartan Life, a time-lapse of Wikipedia's London bombings article being built by users, and the Flaming Lips' free authorized album at 125hz.com. Morgan Spurlock discusses his new FX series 30 Days, describing the minimum-wage, off-the-grid and binge-drinking-mom episodes and screening a confrontational clip from the episode where an ex-Army reservist Christian lives in San Francisco's Castro. Kevin walks through a hack that builds custom Firefox search plugins on top of Google's site: operator, and Brendan Moran files a field piece from the 26th annual Mooning of the Amtrak in Orange County. The Feed covers the scrubbed Discovery launch, NASA's planned lunar reconnaissance camera to photograph Apollo debris, a lawsuit dragging in Archive.org's Wayback Machine, and Pope Benedict XVI's condemnation of Harry Potter. The show ends with a live PSP demo of Death Jr. from producer Chris Charla and Isaac Bender, and a bling-your-gadget segment in which Kevin upstages Sarah's crystal-covered phones with a jeweled Xbox controller.

notable.text: Segment on a video showing Wikipedia's London bombings article evolving in real time, framed as the moment user-created media outpaced mainstream coverage.
The Flaming Lips authorize a free eight-song high-quality MP3 album release at 125hz.com, artwork included.
Archive.org's Wayback Machine is pulled into a Philadelphia trademark case over whether it may archive and serve old public websites without permission.
NASA announces the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera to capture the first recognizable images of Apollo hardware since 1972, aimed at moon-landing conspiracy theorists.
Pope Benedict XVI is revealed to have written, before his election, that the Harry Potter books are capable of corrupting young Christians.

notes.title: Murderball, Fretlight, Comic Life

Paralympian Andy Cohn brings his battered quad rugby chair into the studio to explain the sport behind the documentary Murderball and why the film refuses to treat disability as melodrama. notes.title: ODVD Games, Lollapalooza, Chris Gore
notes.summary: Kevin Pereira and guest co-host Morgan Webb open with Battlefield 2 hackers handing out unearned weapon unlocks on ranked servers, a crowdfunded bounty to reverse-engineer the Nintendo DS's Wi-Fi stack, a Devil's Rejects Flash torture game and a viewer-made Attack of the Show drinking game. The main segments include an interview with CFQ editor Sean Jordan, who discusses the state of TV, and a highly controversial segment with the Flying Spaghetti Monster regarding Kansas's intelligent design law. The episode also covers major news via 'The Feed,' including the AMD vs. Intel processor battle and San Francisco's new gun ban. The latter half focuses heavily on video games, featuring interviews with Neversoft executives Joel Jewett and Scott Pease to demo their Western-themed FPS, 'Gun.'

notable.text: The Flying Spaghetti Monster is interviewed to discuss the Kansas Intelligent Design bill, creating a humorous and absurd debate on creationism.
The Feed reports on San Francisco's new ordinance banning the manufacture, sale, and possession of firearms and ammunition.
The episode features a detailed demo and discussion of the Western-themed FPS 'Gun,' highlighting its cinematic quality and unique approach to the genre.

notes.title: Attack of the Show — 2006-01-05
notes.summary: The first Attack of the Show of 2006, hosted by Kevin Pereira and Brendan Moran. Correspondent Will O'Neill files two live reports from CES in Las Vegas, covering Bill Gates's tenth CES keynote with its family location tracking and surface-computing table demo, the surprise announcement of an external HD DVD drive for the Xbox 360, and Sony's Blu-ray press conference featuring Howard Stringer, Ron Howard, Brian Grazer and Tom Hanks, plus the newly announced Sony Reader. Kristanna Loken visits to promote Uwe Boll's BloodRayne and describes the grueling Romanian night shoot. Eli Roth explains that Hostel grew out of a real Thailand murder-for-hire website Harry Knowles showed him and that Quentin Tarantino offered to finance it himself. Gloria Garayua plays Quake 4 at the LAN party, Blair Butler's Fresh Ink burns All-Star Batman and Robin, and the Feed covers Jon Stewart's likely Oscar hosting gig, Dick Cheney defending warrantless wiretapping, and paid bus tours of Katrina-devastated New Orleans.

notable.text: Microsoft announces at CES that an external HD DVD drive for the Xbox 360 will ship later in 2006, months after the console's launch.
Bill Gates's keynote demos family location sharing, fingerprint login and a table that recognizes a phone and a business card placed on it, framed as realistic 'by the end of the digital decade'.
Sony announces the BDP-S1, its first consumer Blu-ray player, and the Sony Reader e-book device holding 80 books at $300-400.

Eli Roth reveals Hostel was inspired by a real website Harry Knowles found offering the chance to pay $10,000 to shoot someone in Thailand, and that Tarantino called it the sickest idea he had ever heard.
Roth says the Toronto Film Festival screening of Hostel triggered two ambulance calls, a fainting man who fell down an escalator and a woman having a heart attack.
The hosts freeze-frame the Apocalypto trailer to find a single hidden frame of Mel Gibson in a flannel shirt smoking a cigarette.
ABC and ESPN sell 15-minute Rose Bowl highlight downloads on iTunes for $1.99, an early experiment in selling sports to the video iPod.

notes.title: Attack of the Show — 2013-01-08
notes.summary: In this retrospective episode of Attack of the Show hosted by Chris Hardwick titled 'Visionaries', the show looks back at some of the smartest and most influential guests who appeared on the stage. Penn Jillette stops by to discuss atheism and his book 'God, No!'. Bill Nye talks about science education and the controversy surrounding his comments on creationism. Astronaut Mike Massimino shares stories from servicing the Hubble Space Telescope for the IMAX 3D film. Entrepreneur Mark Cuban pontificates on the future of television, and former Community showrunner Dan Harmon opens up about his departure from NBC. Finally, legendary filmmaker James Cameron brings out the custom 3D camera rig used to film Avatar for a special edition of Gadget Pr0n.

notable.text: Steve Wozniak acts as the couch sidekick for the episode.
James Cameron brings the actual 28-pound 3D beam splitter camera rig used on the production of Avatar onto the AOTS set.

The interview traces her journey from her humble beginnings in Oklahoma and Tokyo, through her early acting roles in the Pen 15 Club, to her rise as a major pop culture figure. The conversation delves into her controversial public persona, her extensive magazine career (Playboy and Maxim), and her intense personal struggles, including a notorious incident involving William Shatner. The segment also highlights her philanthropic efforts with the Every Brown Bear Gets a Sandwich Fund and the promotion of her upcoming feature film, complete with a world premiere trailer screening.

Recurring segments like 'Time to Sports' and 'Suits versus Skins' are featured, alongside a deep dive into pop culture trends, such as the iPhone versus iPad debate. The episode celebrates the show's history, featuring characters like Bustis, Office Jesus, and the Zombie plea for tolerance, before concluding with a final sign-off.

notes.title: AOTS - January 23rd, 2013
notes.summary: This historic final episode of Attack of the Show marks the end of G4's flagship series after seven years on the air. Hosted by Matt Mira, Candace Bailey, and Sara Underwood, with 'Weird Al' Yankovic serving as the official show historian, the episode looks back at the show's defining moments, classic clips, and memorable correspondents. Features include an all-time top Around the Net countdown crowning the self-destructing washing machine video, tech and movie wishlist items for 2013, a video message from David Hasselhoff, an In Memoriam segment for past show props, and the tradition of singing 'We Never Got to Dance' with the entire cast and crew. The show concludes with a secret post-credits sketch reuniting original TechTV hosts Kevin Rose and Leo Laporte at The Screensavers set.

notable.text: Series finale of Attack of the Show after seven years on G4 TV.
'Weird Al' Yankovic hosts the cold open and narrates comedic history interludes as 'official show historian'.
Around the Net crowns the famous self-destructing washing machine video as the #1 video in show history.
David Hasselhoff sends a personalized video message wishing the cast and crew well in syndication.
The entire G4 cast and production crew gather on set for the traditional farewell song 'We Never Got to Dance'.
Post-credits epilogue features original TechTV hosts Kevin Rose and Leo Laporte framing the entire 7-year run of G4 as a dream.
